name: Veil Cash
rootCause: Veil.Cash (a zk-SNARK privacy protocol on Base, forked from Tornado Cash) suffered an exploit on its legacy fixed-denomination privacy pools. Due to a misconfigured Groth16 zk-SNARK verifier (where delta2 equaled gamma2), an attacker was able to forge valid zero-knowledge proofs and drain approximately 2.9 ETH (~$5,000) in a single transaction by making multiple fraudulent withdrawals without corresponding deposits. Whitehat interveners and the exploiter voluntarily returned the funds, resulting in 100% recovery. The project’s newer/live pools were unaffected.

descriptions.text: Veil.Cash (a zk-SNARK privacy protocol on Base, forked from Tornado Cash) suffered an exploit on its legacy fixed-denomination privacy pools. Due to a misconfigured Groth16 zk-SNARK verifier (where delta2 equaled gamma2), an attacker was able to forge valid zero-knowledge proofs and drain approximately 2.9 ETH (~$5,000) in a single transaction by making multiple fraudulent withdrawals without corresponding deposits. Whitehat interveners and the exploiter voluntarily returned the funds, resulting in 100% recovery. The project’s newer/live pools were unaffected.

On February 20, 2026, Veil Cash's ETH privacy pool on Base was drained for 2.9 ETH (~$5,700) due to a verifier bug. A Groth16 misconfiguration let an attacker forge zero-knowledge proofs and trigger 29 unbacked withdrawals in a single exploit transaction. The verifier contract was deployed with identical delta and gamma verification key parameters, breaking Groth16 soundness. This let attackers forge proofs and withdraw without any valid deposit.
